scope: IAPP response lifetime while FT AUTH owns exclusive association lease
observations: FT_AuthReqRsnValidation emits automatic key request and may wait 30ms on ack_r1kh under R1KH_HARD_RETRY
wr_ft_peer_enter_locked rejects any existing wr_assoc_event_users for the WCID
wr_ft_peer_leave_locked and wr_ft_peer_advance_locked require exactly one event user
pending first-peer lease also requires exactly one event user at publication, advance and leave
generation retirement/deletion excludes any event users; removing AUTH exclusion while waiting would permit lifetime drift
FT_KDP_KeyResponseToUs mutates PMK-R1 cache before its MAC-only entry lookup and completes the selected entry without request provenance
implementation_constraints: Response claim must bind unique request token and exact BSS/MAC/WCID/generation before any cache mutation
Response lifetime protection must coexist with waiting AUTH without permitting unrelated association/key mutation
Timeout-first and response-first interleavings must balance references without poisoning legitimate AUTH exit
Response must finish cache/counter/completion operations before releasing lifetime protection; AUTH advancement and timeout exit must account for concurrent response ownership
Every delete, reassociation and adapter teardown path must preserve response-held lifetime protection
